meta.title: Install mtmux and open tmux in a browser in 2 minutes
meta.description: Install mtmux with npm, scan the code once, and reach your tmux sessions from any browser. Full CLI reference, self-hosting the broker, and troubleshooting.

hero.title: Two minutes to your first mobile session.
hero.lead: No account, no config file, no reverse proxy. If tmux runs, mtmux attaches.

install.title: Install
install.requirements: Requires Node 22 or newer and tmux. Works on macOS, any glibc or musl Linux, and WSL2. The browser side needs nothing but WebSocket support, which every current browser has — there is no app to install and no account to create.

steps.label: Run it on the machine your tmux server is on
Scan the QR, or type the code at app.mtmux.com
steps.comment: the code is in the URL fragment, never sent to a server

steps.label: You're attached — check or stop the server any time
steps.comment: the browser is trusted from now on

note.label: note
note.body: Run <cmd>mtmux start --local</cmd> to skip the tunnel entirely: it serves loopback and your LAN and contacts no broker at all. <cmd>mtmux local</cmd> is the same thing, shorter.

cli.title: CLI reference
descriptions: Alias for start. Running mtmux with no arguments is the normal way to use it.
Serve this machine's tmux, open a sealed tunnel, and print a QR and a pairing code.
LAN and loopback only. Contacts no broker at all — no traffic leaves your network.
Print the pairing code without the QR block, for terminals that mangle it.
What to call this machine in the dashboard. Pro plans only; Free shows the hostname.
Port to serve on. Defaults to 14100.
Bind address. Defaults to 0.0.0.0 when there is a real LAN, and 127.0.0.1 otherwise.
Don't open a browser on this machine, and print a machine-readable startup record.
Join a pairing the browser started. Prompts for the code if you don't pass one.
Show, or stop, the mtmux server running on this machine.
Check Node, tmux, the tmux socket, the port, config permissions and broker reachability.
Sign in, sign out, or show the signed-in account. Optional — via OAuth device authorization.
List the machines registered to your account.
List the browsers this machine trusts, and forget one by its device id.
Show, regenerate, or set the auth token stored in ~/.mtmux/config.json.
cli.configNote: Configuration lives in <cmd>~/.mtmux/config.json</cmd>, created with mode 0600 — it holds your auth token and device key, so it is deliberately readable only by you.

selfHosting.title: Self-hosting
selfHosting.prose: Two levels, depending on how much of ours you want to use. The first needs no server at all: <cmd>--local</cmd> serves loopback and your LAN, and the CLI never contacts a broker. If you want the tunnel too — reaching the machine from outside your network — run the pairing broker yourself and point the CLI at it.
selfHosting.brokerProse: The broker is <cmd>apps/api</cmd> in the repo. It relays sealed frames and holds no session key, so running your own changes who operates it, not what it can see. <cmd>MTMUX_API_URL</cmd> redirects a single run; <cmd>MTMUX_BUILD_API_URL</cmd> bakes a different default into a build.
selfHosting.localComment: no broker at all — LAN and loopback
selfHosting.runComment: or point the CLI at your own broker
selfHosting.buildComment: or bake it into a build

items.solution: mtmux must run as the user that owns the tmux socket — on a shared box that is the usual cause. <cmd>mtmux doctor</cmd> reports which socket it found and whether it could read it.
A code is single-use and one wrong guess destroys the pairing, by design. mtmux mints a fresh one on its own — check you typed every digit of the newest code on screen, not an earlier one.

items.problem: It printed no code, only local addresses
items.solution: The broker was unreachable, so mtmux degraded to serving your network rather than failing. <cmd>mtmux doctor</cmd> will say so; the LAN URL still works.
Set <cmd>set -g default-terminal "tmux-256color"</cmd> and <cmd>set -as terminal-features ",*:RGB"</cmd> in your tmux.conf.
Either another mtmux is running — <cmd>mtmux status</cmd> will tell you, and <cmd>mtmux stop</cmd> ends it — or something else holds the port, in which case pass <cmd>--port</cmd>.

items.problem: A browser you no longer trust is still paired
items.solution: <cmd>mtmux devices</cmd> lists the device ids this machine trusts, and <cmd>mtmux devices revoke</cmd> forgets one so it cannot reconnect.
